recommendation: Keep this source fix as-is. It is a narrow correction to the original application in an active build page and does not reopen the policy question about whether servers should redirect or canonicalize trailing-slash resource-type requests.
issue_request: FHIR-27113 was Published/Persuasive with Modification for R5 and asked the RESTful HTTP specification to clarify handling of resource type endpoints with a trailing slash, such as [base]/Patient/. The accepted resolution says servers SHALL support both trailing-slash and non-trailing-slash forms if they support either, should not redirect merely to canonicalize the query URL, and may choose their preferred convention for self links.
initial_application: PR HL7/fhir#1124 and commit 819e92b2ed43d416fd6f01342543e90fc4eb3245 added the required paragraph to source/http.html. The approved SHALL, redirect, and canonicalization semantics were present, but the non-trailing example was malformed as [base]/type].
additional_context: source/http.html is in current build scope as the RESTful API page listed in source/hierarchy.xml. The linked Zulip thread supports the intended equivalence/dropped-slash behavior, and the FHIR-I 2020-08-17 minutes record the Persuasive with Modification vote. Searches for later Jira decisions about permanent redirects, canonical query URL, or HTTP identity/trailing slash found no final follow-up changing this rule.
reconciliation: Updated source/http.html to change the malformed non-trailing example to [base]/[type] and lightly cleaned the punctuation in the same sentence so the two examples are parallel and unambiguous. No normative behavior was changed.
source_changes: source/http.html: corrected the malformed non-trailing resource-type URL example from [base]/type] to [base]/[type] in the FHIR-27113 SHALL paragraph.
